web_blocks.title: What Would Have to Change for a Tactical Stage 2 Re-Entry?
paragraphs: Even for short-term momentum traders, MSTX requires three strict preconditions before a tactical trade is valid: (1) MSTR must reclaim its 50-day SMA ($143.26) and 200-day SMA ($132.78) on expanding volume, (2) MSTX must carve out a multi-week Stage 1 floor above $6.72–$8.18 and cross back above its declining 50-day SMA ($15.85) and 30-week SMA ($17.06), and (3) the broader US market must exit its current Correction regime (6 distribution days, below 50-DMA) [20, 21].

web_blocks.html: From a microstructure standpoint, MSTX's classic pivot framework places immediate support at Pivot S1 ($8.18), followed by the 52-week low at $6.72 and Pivot S2 at $4.00 [21, 24]. On the upside, any oversold reflex rally faces dense overhead supply at the 10-day EMA ($11.17), 20-day SMA ($13.20), Pivot Middle ($15.29), 50-day SMA ($15.85), and 30-week SMA ($17.06) [21, 24]. Without a multi-week Stage 1 base above $6.72–$8.18, short-term bounces remain counter-trend rallies inside a primary Stage 4 downtrend.

book_paragraphs: In Chapter 8, you and I step away from SEC filings and look at the cold, hard truth of the price tape. As of Friday, November 13, 2026, MSTX is not merely in a pullback—it is in a full-blown Stan Weinstein Stage 4 waterfall decline. Trading at $8.75, the fund sits 35.57% below its 10-week EMA of $13.58, 44.79% below its 50-day simple moving average of $15.85, 48.71% below its 30-week moving average of $17.06, and 54.21% below its 200-day moving average of $19.11. Every single trend filter—weekly, daily, and 4-hour—is pointing straight down.

Look at the momentum and volatility readings across timeframes. On the 4-hour chart, the 20-EMA sits at $11.19 and the 50-SMA sits at $13.90, with 4H RSI at 30.77 and no intraday turn signal. On the daily chart, RSI is 32.23 and the 14-day Average True Range is $1.79—meaning MSTX's normal daily swing is more than 20% of its share price. Bollinger Band width has blown out to 105.71%, the exact opposite of a tight Volatility Contraction Pattern (VCP). Meanwhile, the fund dropped 5.10% on Friday on 7.19 million shares, 1.06x its 30-day average volume, capping a brutal -24.86% week and -49.01% month.

Notice the broader market context too. Our November 13, 2026 US market ledger places the S&P 500 and Nasdaq in a Correction regime—below the 50-day moving average with six distribution days and market breadth above the 50-DMA sitting at 52.6%. When the broad market itself is under institutional distribution, high-beta crypto proxies do not quietly form durable bottoms; they suffer forced margin liquidations and air-pocket gaps. And notice that underlying MSTR ($111.62) is itself trapped below both its 50-day SMA ($143.26) and its 200-day SMA ($132.78), while spot IBIT ($38.94) sits below its 50-day ($45.47) and 200-day ($41.06) averages. There is zero relative strength anywhere in the complex.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION
book_callouts.text: When an ETF has a 20.5% daily ATR and trades 49% below its 30-week moving average, 'buying the dip' isn't value investing—it is stepping in front of a freight train without a floor.

book_subsections.title: Why We Block Call Options Here Too
paragraphs: Some traders look at an RSI of 32 and immediately reach for call options to 'catch the bounce' with limited dollars. Our options engine checked the MSTX chain and found 154.9% at-the-money implied volatility matching 154.9% 20-day realized volatility, alongside illiquid or zero-bid quotes on post-split strikes. More importantly, our fundamental safety interlock stamps NO OPTIONS EDGE whenever Pass 1 rates a vehicle FUNDAMENTAL FAIL.

Think about why that rule exists: buying a call option on a 2x daily-reset ETF in Stage 4 layers two forms of decay on top of each other—options theta decay and daily-reset volatility slippage—while you fight a wall of overhead supply between $11.17 and $19.11. Even if MSTX bounces 15% for two days, high implied volatility and wide post-split bid-ask spreads can leave call buyers with barely a scratch of profit before the downtrend resumes.

What would have to change for even a tactical short-term trader to look at MSTX again? Three things: first, the US market must exit Correction via a confirmed Follow-Through Day; second, MSTR must reclaim its 200-day moving average ($132.78) and 50-day moving average ($143.26) on expanding institutional volume; and third, MSTX must carve out a multi-week Stage 1 base above $6.72 to $8.18 and cross back above a flattening 30-week moving average ($17.06). Until all three happen, the tape says one word: stay away.

book_subsections.title: Mapping Overhead Supply and Why 'Oversold' Can Stay Oversold
paragraphs: Beginners often look at a daily RSI of 32.23 and a 4-hour RSI of 30.77 and assume a snapback rally is guaranteed. In Stage 2 uptrends, an RSI near 30 is often a buying opportunity at a rising 50-day moving average. In Stage 4 downtrends, however, oversold readings are a symptom of persistent institutional distribution, not a floor. Look at the sheer wall of trapped buyers sitting above $8.75: anyone who bought MSTX at the 10-day EMA ($11.17), the 20-day SMA ($13.20), the 50-day SMA ($15.85), or the 30-week SMA ($17.06) is underwater and eager to sell into any bounce.

Meanwhile, on the downside, Pivot S1 sits just pennies away at $8.18, followed by the 52-week low of $6.72 and Pivot S2 at $4.00. Notice how wide the daily swings are: a 14-day ATR of $1.79 means MSTX can move 20% in a single session on normal 7-million-share volume. Trying to time a multi-day swing in that environment is pure coin-flipping against an unfavorable drift.

book_subsections.title: Volume, Liquidity, and the Illusion of Institutional Sponsorship
paragraphs: When you see 7.19 million shares trading on a Friday in MSTX—roughly $63 million of daily dollar turnover—it is tempting to assume 'institutions are accumulating here.' Don't confuse high trading volume with institutional accumulation. In a leveraged single-stock ETF, high volume in a Stage 4 downtrend is driven by retail dip-buyers, short-term momentum algorithms, options market makers delta-hedging, and authorized participants creating or redeeming baskets to arbitrage the 4:00 PM ET reset.

True institutional sponsorship shows up as rising relative strength, tight weekly price contractions near 52-week highs, and expanding up-volume above a rising 30-week moving average. MSTX exhibits the exact opposite: a 105.71% Bollinger Band width, a -89.47% drawdown from its 52-week high of $83.10, and persistent distribution below every moving average on the chart.
